metrics.name: Total Revenue
metrics.definition: Sum of total_amount from non-cancelled orders

metrics.name: Order Cancellation Rate
metrics.calculation: 100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Cancelled') / COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce.orders

metrics.name: Payment Success Rate
metrics.calculation: 100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Success') / COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce.payments

metrics.name: Average Product Rating
metrics.definition: Mean star rating across all reviews (1-5 scale)

metrics.name: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)
metrics.definition: Total spend per customer across all non-cancelled orders
metrics.calculation: SUM(total_amount) per user_id FROM ecommerce.orders WHERE status != 'Cancelled'

common_gotchas.solution: Always filter WHERE status != 'Cancelled' when calculating revenue or order metrics

common_gotchas.issue: Using product.price instead of order_items.unit_price for revenue
common_gotchas.solution: unit_price in order_items is the price at time of purchase. Product.price may have changed since. Always use order_items.unit_price for revenue calculations.

common_gotchas.issue: Assuming all orders have shipping records
common_gotchas.solution: Only orders with status 'Shipped' or 'Delivered' have rows in shipping_details. LEFT JOIN if you need all orders.

common_gotchas.issue: Payment status vs order status mismatch
common_gotchas.solution: Cancelled orders typically have Failed payments, but Pending orders may have Pending payments. Don't assume a 1:1 status mapping.
No unique constraint on (product_id, user_id) in reviews. A user could review the same product multiple times. Use DISTINCT or latest review if needed.

common_gotchas.issue: All tables are in the 'ecommerce' schema, not 'public'
common_gotchas.solution: Always prefix table names with 'ecommerce.' (e.g., ecommerce.orders, ecommerce.users). Queries without the schema prefix will fail.
